paragraphs: A bodybuilder is a useful base figure for a reason that has nothing to do with the sport: every muscle group is legible under the skin, so the mesh reads correctly under any lighting and deforms predictably when rigged. It is anatomy made visible without stripping anything away.
The character holds 92,072 polygons and 49,258 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied in a T pose ready for your own rig, and carries StemCell certification.
At $149 it suits game characters, fitness and sports visualisation, anatomy and figure reference, advertising, film previsualisation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

The Wedgetail is an airliner with a radar bolted to its spine, and the shape of that antenna is why it looks wrong at first glance. It is fixed rather than rotating, which is unusual for airborne early warning, and Australia was the first air force to make the type work operationally.

The airframe holds 623,033 polygons and 643,931 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 26 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $149 it suits defence and aviation visualisation, flight simulation, documentary and news graphics, film and game environments. On sale since 2019.

The extended range 777 changed what a twin engined aircraft was allowed to do. Once regulators accepted that two engines could cross an ocean, the four engined fleet started disappearing, and this is the aeroplane that made the argument.

The airframe holds 1,260,204 polygons and 735,999 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and comes rigged so the gear and control surfaces can be posed or animated. Native rigged builds for Maya and Cinema 4D are offered separately.
At $149 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits flight simulation, airline and airport visualisation, documentary and news graphics, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The Dreamliner's wing is its tell: composite, thin, and visibly flexed upward in cruise in a way aluminium never allowed. Qatar Airways flies the type on routes that only make sense with that efficiency, and the burgundy tail is one of the more disciplined liveries in the business.

The airframe holds 431,697 polygons and 442,157 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 32 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $149 it suits flight simulation, airline and airport visualisation, travel advertising, film backgrounds and editorial illustration. On sale since 2018.

The Stratotanker has been refuelling aircraft in flight since the jet age began, and it is still doing it. The flying boom under the tail, operated by a crew member lying prone at the back, is a piece of engineering that has outlasted almost everything it was designed to serve.

The airframe holds 179,181 polygons and 196,528 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification for use across engines and renderers. A rigged build is offered separately.
At $149 it suits defence and aviation visualisation, flight simulation, documentary and news graphics, film and game environments. On sale since 2021.

BYD's DM-i system is a hybrid built the other way round: the engine mostly generates rather than drives, and the car behaves like an electric one until the battery runs low. The Qin L is where that packaging meets a conventional saloon body, and it is a large part of why Chinese hybrids undercut everyone on running cost.
The model holds 213,482 polygons and 237,355 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in Space Black. Native rigged builds for Cinema 4D and Maya are offered separately.

At $149 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits automotive marketing and configurators, street and architectural scenes, advertising, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A fish swimming is a whole body wave, not a tail flick. Getting that right is the difference between an aquarium shot that reads and one that looks like a toy being dragged through water, and it is why an animated build is worth more than a posed one.
This build is prepared for Maya, rigged and animated with a swim cycle, so it opens as a native scene rather than an import. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $149 it suits underwater and marine visualisation, aquarium and nature documentary work, fishing and seafood presentation, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

Traditional Chinese dress is cut to hang rather than to fit, and a walking pose is the only way to show that: the fabric moves independently of the body, which is exactly what a standing figure cannot demonstrate.
The character holds 35,576 polygons and 37,159 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, light enough for crowds and background use, and carries StemCell certification.
At $149 it suits cultural and historical visualisation, architectural and urban scenes, film previsualisation, education and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

Fuxing means rejuvenation, and the CR400 was the point at which China stopped licensing high speed train designs from abroad and started exporting its own. The nose shape is the visible part of that: sculpted entirely for tunnel pressure waves rather than for looks.
The model is dense at 2,777,896 polygons and 1,415,801 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification for use across engines and renderers.
At $149 it suits rail and transport visualisation, infrastructure and urban scenes, documentary and news graphics, advertising, film and game environments. On sale since 2023.

The open top tour bus is the same vehicle in every city on earth, which is the point: a tourist recognises it before reading the destination board. The upper deck has no roof because the whole product is the view, and the route is a loop rather than a line.
The model holds 435,138 polygons and 246,810 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, suited to the repeated seating and panelling, and carries StemCell certification.
At $149 it suits urban and architectural visualisation, tourism and travel imagery, advertising, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

A piling rig in working position is a different machine from one in transport: the mast is up, the leader is plumbed, and the whole weight distribution has changed. Bauer builds these for foundation work, where the hole in the ground eventually becomes a building.

The model holds 359,156 polygons and 379,178 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 19 maps, 13 at 4096x4096, 4 at 2048x2048 and 2 at 1024x1024. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $149 it suits construction and civil engineering visualisation, equipment marketing, training and safety material, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2018.

A barge is a hull and nothing else. No engine, no accommodation, no bow to speak of: it exists to be pushed, and an empty one riding high with the hold open shows the whole point of the design in a way a loaded one never does.

The model holds 264,772 polygons and 300,901 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, suited to the repeated plating, and is supplied empty with the hold open. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $149 it suits river and port visualisation, logistics and shipping presentation, industrial and infrastructure scenes, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2026.

The head is where anatomy and likeness meet. Every muscle under the skin has a visible consequence on the surface, and modelling both layers together is the only way to explain why an expression looks the way it does rather than simply reproducing it.

The model holds 196,594 polygons and 195,407 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the full anatomy together with the skin surface. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $149 it suits medical and dental education, surgical and aesthetic visualisation, anatomy reference for artists, character work and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

Taiwan built the Ching-kuo because it could not buy what it needed. Denied foreign fighters, the island designed its own, and the result is a compact aircraft assembled from what was available under an embargo rather than from a clean sheet of requirements.

This is the simplified build, 142,231 polygons and 146,735 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, deliberately lighter for scenes where the aircraft is not the focus. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $149 it suits defence and aviation visualisation, flight simulation, documentary and news graphics, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.
